approved: Milton Dick In accordance with the resolution agreed to on 28 May 2026, Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027 is returned to the House for further consideration. The original question was that this bill be now read a second time. To this the honourable member for Ryan has moved as an amendment that all words after 'That' be omitted with a view to substituting other words. The question now is that the amendment be agreed to.

Sue Lines I will first deal with the second reading amendment circulated by the Australian Greens. The question is that the amendment on sheet 3861 be agreed to. _Australian Greens_ _' circulated_ _amendment—_ At the end of the motion, add ", but the Senate: (a) notes that: (i) Australia is one of the world's largest exporters of gas, yet multinational gas corporations are making extraordinary profits while offshore projects get our gas for free, (ii) introducing a minimum tax rate of at least 25% on gas export revenue would ensure that big gas corporations pay their fair share and raise an estimated $17 billion per year in public revenue, and (iii) this revenue could be invested in cost of living support, accelerating the transition to clean energy and properly funding essential public services, including the National Disability Insurance Scheme; and (b) calls on the Government to reverse all cuts to the National Disability Insurance Scheme included in these bills".

Sue Lines I will now deal with the second reading amendment circulated by One Nation. The question is that the amendment on sheet 3858 be agreed to. _One Nation's_ _circulated_ _amendment—_ Omit all words after "That", substitute "further consideration of the bills be made an order of the day for the first sitting day after amendments are circulated removing all funding for net zero measures and the administration of net zero measures". _A division having been called and the bells being rung—_ David Pocock by leave—I was just wondering if my support for (a) on that last amendment could be noted. Sue Lines On 3861? David Pocock Yes.

Moved the second reading of Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2026-2027, seeking $33.7 billion from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for non-ordinary government services in 2026-27, including defence, housing, infrastructure and an Advance to the Finance Minister of $3.6 billion.

Declared that Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2026-2027 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027 stood referred to the Federation Chamber immediately, with Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026 referred at the adjournment of its second reading debate.

Moved to schedule consideration of three appropriation bills across portfolios and timeframes, then proposed requiring responsible ministers to attend; the amendment was negatived and the original motion agreed to.
Reported that Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027 had been returned for further consideration and that an amendment moved by the member for Ryan was before the House.

Moved that the 2026-27 appropriation bills be read a second time and incorporated their speeches in Hansard. The bills seek $178.7 billion, $33.7 billion and $345.4 million for ordinary government services, non-ordinary services and parliamentary departments, including funding for health, Defence, housing, infrastructure and an Advance to the Finance Minister.
